sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer / TSL; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel shading, ink outlines, warm desert colors; procedural 3D models
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack; procedural flight banking and effects
sourceInformation.audio: Code-synthesized arcade music (10% default), rotor, weapons, explosions and Animalese-style gibberish radio; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Protocol v1 ghost score competition for 1–4; standalone two-pilot local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium with software WebGPU, scripted campaign and feature checks, emulated standard gamepads, touch profiles, Web Audio analyser, AI Hub harness
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge. Retrieved only requested AI Hub integration source and pinned software dependencies

testingFeedback: Five game issues found and fixed: graphics-device loss, short weapon taps, effect aging during fast-forward, stale boss state on restart, and mouse hover interfering with controller focus. Test-runner setup and timing problems were also corrected.
One game-breaking graphics issue: losing the WebGPU device could leave a blank scene. Automatic display recovery through Three.js WebGL 2 compatibility is now tested.

The fixed-timestep full campaign playthrough: all three sectors, five rescues, rockets, flares, the boss second phase, and victory. Hub conformance tests with packet loss also verified multiplayer lifecycle.
Early tests that used short wall-clock sleeps for controller input produced timing failures on the software renderer; waiting for actual input sampling was more useful.
engineFeedback: TSL banded lighting and Three.js AnimationMixer made procedural models, cel shading and rotor animation work within one engine on both rendering backends.
Guessed wrong about software WebGPU stability and effect lifetimes during fast-forward. Added explicit device-loss recovery and fixed-timestep effect aging.
The arcade flight and combat systems, convoy AI, hover rescue and resupply, campaign director, controller menus, procedural audio and ghost synchronization.
Coordinating asynchronous graphics startup, fixed Rapier physics, native animation and browser input across play, pause, attract and Hub lifecycle states.
none; used the published engines unmodified. The application adds renderer recovery and custom TSL materials.
A built-in WebGPU cel material with ink outlines and automatic device-loss recovery.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source, complete vertical-slice requirement and controller-first direction gave a clear design target.

The no-research instruction alongside a required remote integration, and whether standalone multiplayer had to be internet multiplayer. Integration files and dependencies were treated as implementation inputs; standalone play uses couch co-op.
Combining polished procedural visuals and sound, a complete campaign, native input, developer tools and Hub sessions in one offline HTML file.
Clarify whether standalone multiplayer means local co-op, internet play or both, and explicitly allow retrieval of required integration files separately from research.

aiHub.name: Chopper Caboodle
aiHub.tagline: A little chopper. A whole lot of trouble.
aiHub.description: Protect a desert convoy in a cel-shaded helicopter arcade romp. Rescue crew, unleash rockets and flares, and face the Dustmaker solo, in couch co-op, or in AI Hub ghost score races.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD fly; right stick / mouse aim; R2 / Space / LMB fire; Square / E rockets; Circle / Q flares; L3 / Shift boost; hover low to rescue and resupply.
